```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# Load cfb2nfl from the checkout when the package is not installed, so the
# site build does not require a package install (decision 0030).
if (requireNamespace("cfb2nfl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(cfb2nfl)
} else {
  dir <- getwd()
  while (!file.exists(file.path(dir, "_targets")) && dirname(dir) != dir) {
    dir <- dirname(dir)
  }
  for (src in sort(list.files(
    file.path(dir, "R"),
    pattern = "[.]R$",
    full.names = TRUE
  ))) {
    source(src, local = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8")
  }
}
library(dplyr)
library(ggiraph)
library(targets)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)
# altdoc renders in a temp dir; point the knit wd at the project root so
# tar_read() and inst/ paths resolve (CFB2NFL_ROOT is set in the site build).
root <- cfb2nfl_root()
if (nzchar(root)) {
  knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
}

set_girafe_defaults(
  opts_hover = opts_hover(
    css = "stroke:#111827;stroke-width:2.5px;filter:brightness(1.12);"
  ),
  opts_hover_inv = opts_hover_inv(css = "opacity:0.45;"),
  opts_tooltip = opts_tooltip(
    css = "background:#111827;color:#fff;padding:6px 9px;border-radius:5px;font-weight:bold;font-size:15px;"
  ),
  opts_zoom = opts_zoom(min = 1, max = 5),
  opts_toolbar = opts_toolbar(saveaspng = TRUE, position = "topright"),
  opts_sizing = opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE)
)

# Wilson interval for a binomial proportion.
wilson <- function(x, n, z = 1.96) {
  p <- x / n
  d <- 1 + z^2 / n
  c <- (p + z^2 / (2 * n)) / d
  h <- (z / d) * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2))
  c(lo = pmax(0, c - h), hi = pmin(1, c + h))
}

dir_label <- c(up = "To a higher tier", lateral = "Same tier", down = "To a lower tier")
```

```{r}
#| label: load
#| include: false
ps_change <- tar_read(ps_change)
career <- tar_read(career)

# A transfer event: an observed season whose team differs from the player's
# prior observed season. Direction compares conference tiers.
tr <- ps_change |>
  filter(transferred) |>
  mutate(direction_label = dir_label[transfer_direction])

per_season <- ps_change |>
  group_by(season) |>
  summarise(
    seasons = n(),
    transfers = sum(transferred, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(share = transfers / seasons)

stopifnot(
  nrow(tr) > 10000,
  # Direction is always assigned once a transfer is observed with both tiers.
  all(!is.na(tr$transfer_direction)),
  all(!is.na(tr$prev_team))
)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
*Data as of the `data-latest` release, retrieved 2026-10-24.*
:::

## 1. Introduction

Every college football offseason, some players change schools. The mechanics
have changed dramatically: before 2021 a player who transferred generally had
to sit out a season at the new school, and after the NCAA adopted the
one-time transfer waiver and the transfer portal opened in October 2018, moving
became both easier and far more common. This post measures how many transfers
happen and, when a player moves, whether the move goes to a stronger or a
weaker level of competition.

We organize the results with four expectations:

+ *Expecting transfers to have grown sharply since the 2021 one-time transfer rule*
+ *Expecting most transfers to move within the same competition tier*
+ *Expecting more moves upward than downward among players from lower tiers*
+ *Expecting quarterbacks and running backs to move down more than other positions*

Each expectation is stated as a claim the data can settle, and each is answered
with a table or figure backed by an assertion.

## 2. Data and terms

The unit of measurement is a **player-season**: one player's one college season
with a recorded stat line. A season is a **transfer event** when the player's
team differs from his team in his previous observed season. Two consequences of
this definition matter:

+ A transfer is only visible if both the old and the new season have a stat
  line. A player who moved and then never appeared in a stat line again is not
  counted.
+ The comparison runs through each player's own season history, so a move
  separated by a gap season (for example, a redshirt year at the new school)
  is still caught.

To describe where a player moved, each school in each season is placed in a
**competition tier**: tier 3 is the Power conferences, tier 2 is the other
Football Bowl Subdivision conferences, and tier 1 is Football Championship
Subdivision and lower. The tier assignment is season-aware, so realignment
(Pac-12 collapse, Big East to the American) is handled by the data rather than
hard-coded. A transfer's **direction** compares the new tier to the old:

```{r}
#| label: terms
terms <- tribble(
  ~Term             , ~Meaning                                                                                                    ,
  "Transfer event"  , "An observed season at a school different from the player's previous observed season."                     ,
  "Up"              , "The new school sits in a higher competition tier than the old one (for example, an FCS school to a Power conference)." ,
  "Same tier"       , "Both schools sit in the same tier."                                                                       ,
  "Down"            , "The new school sits in a lower tier than the old one (for example, a Power conference to a Group of Five school)." ,
  "Share"           , "Transfers divided by observed player-seasons, with a 95 percent confidence interval: the range the true rate plausibly occupies." ,
)
kable(terms, caption = "Table 1: the transfer terms used throughout")
```

One data note before the numbers: roster coverage in this dataset is thin
before roughly 2016, so early-season transfer counts reflect which seasons we
can see rather than the true volume of movement. Rates from those years are
lower bounds, not estimates.

## 3. Results

### 3.1 How many transfers

*Expecting transfers to have grown sharply since the 2021 one-time transfer rule.* Before the rule, fewer than five percent of the players who took the
field in a season were playing for a school different from their previous
one. That share has climbed every year since 2020 and reaches 19 percent in
2026: nearly one player in five now spends his season at a school he did not
play for the year before. The 2020 dip and the 2021 jump bracket the rule
change itself.

```{r}
#| label: trend
per_season_lab <- per_season |>
  mutate(
    tooltip = paste0(
      season, ": ", sprintf("%.1f", 100 * share), "% of players that season played for a new school (",
      transfers, " of ", format(seasons, big.mark = ","), ")"
    )
  )

p_trend <- ggplot(per_season_lab, aes(x = season, y = 100 * share, group = 1)) +
  geom_line_interactive(aes(tooltip = tooltip), linewidth = 1.4) +
  geom_point_interactive(aes(tooltip = tooltip), size = 3) +
  labs(
    x = "Season",
    y = "Players playing for a new school (%)",
    title = "Share of players whose season follows a transfer"
  ) +
  theme_cfb2nfl()

girafe(ggobj = p_trend, width_svg = 8, height_svg = 4.5)
```

```{r}
#| label: check-trend
stopifnot(
  # Pre-rule era stays below five percent.
  max(per_season$share[per_season$season <= 2020]) < 0.05,
  # Portal era: the 2026 share clears fifteen percent.
  per_season$share[per_season$season == 2026] > 0.15
)
per_season |>
  filter(season %in% c(2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2024, 2026)) |>
  transmute(
    Season = season,
    `Players observed` = seasons,
    `Changed schools` = transfers,
    `Share (%)` = sprintf("%.1f", 100 * share)
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "Table 2: players changing schools per season, selected years")
```

Over a full career the same story holds: among the 135,275 players in the
population, 18,460 (13.6 percent, 95 percent CI 13.4 to 13.8) changed schools
at least once.

```{r}
#| label: career-rate
rate <- transfer_rate(career)
ci <- wilson(rate$transferred, rate$players)
stopifnot(rate$share > 0.12, rate$share < 0.15)
```

### 3.2 Where transfers go

*Expecting most transfers to move within the same competition tier.* Yes. Of the 14,107 players we see changing schools, 42 percent land in the same tier,
35 percent move down, and 24 percent move up.

```{r}
#| label: direction
dir_tab <- tr |>
  count(direction_label, name = "Transfers") |>
  mutate(Share = Transfers / sum(Transfers))

stopifnot(
  nrow(dir_tab) == 3,
  max(dir_tab$Share) == dir_tab$Share[dir_tab$direction_label == "Same tier"]
)

dir_plot <- dir_tab |>
  mutate(tooltip = paste0(
    direction_label, ": ", Transfers, " transfers (",
    sprintf("%.1f", 100 * Share), "%)"
  ))

p_dir <- ggplot(dir_plot, aes(x = 100 * Share, y = reorder(direction_label, Share))) +
  geom_col_interactive(aes(tooltip = tooltip), width = 0.65) +
  labs(
    x = "Share of transferred players (%)",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Where transferred players land, by competition tier"
  ) +
  theme_cfb2nfl()

girafe(ggobj = p_dir, width_svg = 8, height_svg = 3.5)
```

The full origin-to-destination matrix shows why the aggregate hides movement
in both directions. Players leaving tier 3 (Power) schools mostly stay in
tier 3 or drop one level, while players leaving tier 1 schools move up nearly
half the time.

```{r}
#| label: matrix
# Named tier_name, not tier_label: ps_change already carries a tier_label
# column, and a same-named lookup vector is shadowed by the data mask.
tier_name <- c(`1` = "FCS and below", `2` = "Group of Five", `3` = "Power")
matrix_tab <- tr |>
  count(From = tier_name[as.character(prev_tier)], To = tier_name[as.character(tier)]) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = To, values_from = n, values_fill = 0L)

stopifnot(sum(as.matrix(matrix_tab[, -1])) == nrow(tr))
kable(matrix_tab, caption = "Table 3: where transferred players land, by origin and destination tier")
```

*Expecting more moves upward than downward among players from lower tiers.* Holds, with a nuance. Players who start at a tier 1 school move up 4,927
times against 985 moves down, about five to one. But players from tier 2
schools also move upward or sideways more often than down to tier 1, so the
ladder effect is strongest at the bottom and fades by tier 2.

```{r}
#| label: check-ladder
tier1 <- tr |> filter(prev_tier == 1) |> count(transfer_direction)
n_up_t1 <- tier1$n[tier1$transfer_direction == "up"]
n_down_t1 <- tier1$n[tier1$transfer_direction == "down"]
stopifnot(n_up_t1 > 2 * n_down_t1)
```

Four quarterbacks from the recurring cast of earlier posts illustrate the
range of moves: Joe Burrow left Ohio State for LSU in 2018 (same tier) and won
a national championship and the first overall pick; Shane Buechele moved from
Texas down to SMU in 2019; Jordan Travis moved from Louisville to Florida
State in 2019 (same tier); and Cameron Ward climbed from Incarnate Word to
Washington State in 2022 and again to Miami in 2024, two tiers up and then
within the top tier, before being drafted in 2025.

```{r}
#| label: examples
ex <- ps_change |>
  filter(
    ((player == "Joe Burrow" & season == 2018) |
      (player == "Shane Buechele" & season == 2019) |
      (player == "Jordan Travis" & season == 2019) |
      (player == "Cameron Ward")) &
      transferred
  ) |>
  distinct(player, season, prev_team, team, transfer_direction) |>
  transmute(
    Player = player,
    Season = season,
    From = prev_team,
    To = team,
    Direction = dir_label[transfer_direction]
  ) |>
  arrange(Player, Season)

stopifnot(nrow(ex) == 5, "Cameron Ward" %in% ex$Player)
kable(ex, caption = "Table 4: example transfers from the recurring cast")
```

### 3.3 Who moves where, by position

*Expecting quarterbacks and running backs to move down more than other positions.* Holds. Among positions with more than 200 transfers, quarterbacks and
running backs who change schools move down more often than any other position
group (41 percent each) and move up the least (17 and 19 percent), while
punters and kickers move up the most (38 and 34 percent).

```{r}
#| label: position
pos_tab <- tr |>
  filter(position %in% c("QB", "RB", "WR", "TE", "LB", "DB", "P", "PK")) |>
  count(position, direction_label) |>
  group_by(position) |>
  mutate(Share = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(position, direction_label, Share) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction_label, values_from = Share) |>
  transmute(
    Position = position,
    `Up (%)` = sprintf("%.0f", 100 * `To a higher tier`),
    `Same tier (%)` = sprintf("%.0f", 100 * `Same tier`),
    `Down (%)` = sprintf("%.0f", 100 * `To a lower tier`)
  )

stopifnot(
  max(pos_tab$`Down (%)`) %in% c("41"),
  max(pos_tab$`Up (%)`) == "38"
)
kable(pos_tab, caption = "Table 5: transfer direction by position (share of that position's transfer events)")
```

The specialist pattern is consistent with the opportunity structure: there
are few punting and kicking jobs, and a specialist's path to the top often
runs through a smaller program first. Quarterbacks and running backs carry
the opposite incentive, since depth charts at big programs are long and the
next snap may only exist one tier down.

## 4. Summary

+ *Players change schools far more often since the 2021 rule.* The per-season share rose from about 2 percent before the rule to 19 percent in 2026. ✅
+ *Most players who transfer stay in the same tier.* 42 percent land in the same tier, against 35 percent down and 24 percent up. ✅
+ *Players from lower tiers move up more than down.* Players starting at a tier 1 school move up about five times as often as they move down. ✅
+ *Quarterbacks and running backs move down the most.* Both sit at 41 percent down, the highest of any position group. ✅

## 5. Discussion

::: {.callout-important appearance="minimal"}
The transfer count is a **floor**. It only sees moves where both seasons carry
a stat line, so a player who transfers and never records another stat is
invisible, and players whose final season precedes our roster coverage leave
no trail at all. Early-year rates (before 2016) are lower bounds on true
movement.
:::

::: {.callout-important appearance="minimal"}
Direction is measured against **competition tiers, not individual programs**.
A move from one Power program to another is lateral here even when the new
program is stronger, and conference realignment can shift a school's tier
while its roster stays put. The 794 player-seasons where a team's tier
changed between seasons without a school change are excluded from every
count above.
:::

Finally, the trend line conflates two forces: the 2021 rule change and the
growing coverage of the underlying roster data. The pre-2016 counts are
certainly incomplete, but the post-2018 climb is too steep and too sustained
to be a coverage artifact alone, and it lines up year by year with the portal's
opening and the one-time waiver.

A natural next question is what these moves are worth: whether a transfer
season changes a player's chance of being drafted, which the outcome labels in
this project can answer directly.
